summary.intent: Update Claude Code to the latest version, migrate from deprecated npm installation to the native installer, then run a full development retrospective to prune knowledge graph files, propagate updated metrics to core documentation files, and persist learnings to SurrealDB and the Obsidian vault.
summary.outcome: Claude Code was successfully updated from v2.1.105 to v2.1.112 and migrated from the deprecated npm/Linuxbrew installation to the native installer. The retrospective completed all steps: KEY_LEARNINGS.md compressed 48% (382→197 lines), MISSION_JOURNAL.md updated with 5 new sessions, CLAUDE.md and CAPABILITY_MAP_REDUX.md corrected with accurate metrics, SurrealDB crash loop fixed and learnings persisted, and 3 vault entries created.

repo: Skills have grown from 206 to 235 .md files (+14%) and PRIME-tagged skills from 151 to 215 since last retrospective — metrics drift ~2-4% per session without active propagation passes.
MCP tools count was severely understated in CLAUDE.md (41+ claimed vs 87 actual), likely because the count wasn't being tracked systematically.
Genesis tests grew from 348 to 398 and JEPA tests from 9 to 34 — the JEPA count discrepancy suggests a test suite was added without updating docs.
Skill registry JSON (133 entries) is significantly out of sync with actual .md skill files (235) — registry regeneration is needed.
KEY_LEARNINGS.md uses a 'temporal decay' compression strategy: recent sessions (85+) kept at full detail, older sessions compressed to single-line summaries while preserving L### reference numbers.

SurrealDB has two separate graph systems: neurons/synapses (vault-keeper domain for Graph HIHO) and prompt_artifacts/universe_snapshots (genesis execution). journey_transitions and prompt_artifacts tables don't exist in the main namespace.
The Obsidian vault is the offline-first source of truth; SurrealDB adds graph querying but vault works without it.

code.finding: Compressed from 382 to 197 lines (48% reduction) by converting verbose multi-paragraph old-session entries to single-line summaries; all L### reference numbers preserved.
Added Sessions 97-101 entries; compressed bottom entries to stay near 150-line soft target (ended at 154 lines).
Stale metrics and completed Next Steps updated; stays under 200-line limit at 163 lines.
Six metric discrepancies corrected: tests 6356→6369, skills 206→235 (151→215 PRIME), MCP tools 41+→87, API routes 93→92, genesis tests 348→398, JEPA tests 9→34.
Synced to match corrected CLAUDE.md metrics.

workflow: SurrealDB 3.0 requires the --temporary-directory path to pre-exist; after /tmp cleanup or reboot the directory is gone, causing exit code 2 crash loop. Fix: mkdir -p /tmp/surrealdb + systemctl --user reset-failed + start.
After systemd crash-loops a service into the 'failed' state, systemctl --user reset-failed <service> is required before a new start attempt will succeed.
Claude Code npm installation bundles ripgrep internally; removing the npm package breaks the Grep tool in the current session. Self-heals on restart with native binary.
Native Claude Code installer places binary at ~/.local/bin/claude as a symlink to ~/.local/share/claude/versions/<version>; auto-updates re-point the symlink — enables instant rollback.
When two Claude Code installations exist (npm-global + native), whichever is first on $PATH wins — can silently fall back to older version if PATH ordering changes.
The compound engineering feedback loop: session learnings → KEY_LEARNINGS → CLAUDE.md → future sessions. Without retrospective passes, documentation falls ~2-4% behind per session.

friction: SurrealDB was crash-looping due to missing /tmp/surrealdb directory — required diagnosing systemd logs, identifying the root cause, and resetting the failure counter before the service would start.

npm uninstall of Claude Code appeared to fail initially, causing a redundant verification step before confirming it had actually succeeded.

journey_transitions and prompt_artifacts tables are missing from the main SurrealDB namespace — may require schema migration or are in a different DB, blocking full retrospective persistence.
